newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields end up on liquidity worries.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields end up on liquidity worries.

text.p: Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds closed higher on Friday as fears spread over possible tightening of liquidity after the Lunar New Year holidays, traders said.
But yields on three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) dropped as short-term liquidity remained abundant.
* 3-yr corporates close at 12.00 pct vs 11.97 pct
* 3-mth CDs end at 12.35 pct vs 12.50 pct
* Overnight average call rates at 12.2 pct vs 12.3 pct
"It was as expected, although it would pressure the market," said one broker.
New issues were estimated at 41 billion won on Friday, compared with 79 billion on Thursday.
Traders expected the bond yields to trade between 11.95 to 12.10 percent next week.
Yields on three-month certificates of deposit dropped as the short-term liquidity remained high.
"Banks preferred to invest in shorter-term intruments than corporate bonds," another broker said.
